review: I really just want to know... Why would you make almost exactly the same mistake twice? You guys literally did the same exact thing that killed BLC... I came back after a year break to find no player base and items? Are you seriously kidding me? Serves you right I guess for pumping so much into that stupid battle royale game that everyone at the time thought was going to be a part of Battlerite. You guys had a great game. I played all through early access, through the free to play release, through all of the characters (except Shen Rao) and it's sad that you guys made such terrible decisions to kill our game. I don't normally write reviews but I had to in this case because it was my absolute favorite MOBA and before this it was BLC. I will never again spend money on a Stunlock Studio game because I know it has a maximum of 2-3 year shelf life due to incompetent leadership.

Imagine if Albert Einstein gave up on his career in physics to pursue a career of burger flipping

That's essentially what happened to Battlerite

Sometimes i queue up just to reminisce about the old days, and even though I know there will be no one else in the championship league that never resets, I'll spend half an hour searching for games before leaving. I miss it so much.

It's honestly a shame that more people don't know the name Stunlock Studio. 

I feel like the lack of people talking about how badly they fucked this up stems entirely from nobody realizing what they did. These guys had the best battle arena game ever, bar none, literally zero competition at the time or since that comes even remotely close and they blew it. TWICE.

Bloodline Champions was amazing. It died. Battlerite was a resurrection of Bloodline Champions under a new IP to 'escape the limitations of a publisher' and I was fucking ecstatic over that because it was everything I remembered and more. 

Guess how that played out? They let it die. And why did they let it die? Why, to chase Battle Royale money of course. What else? Make a new 'battle royale' mode in the dedicated arena pvp game, fail to deliver updates of any kind to the actual gameplay, and then make people pay for the 'new mode' because it's actually a new game and... oh hey look it didn't gain traction and died like the vast majority of other BRs that followed the trend. Who could have seen this coming?

It's just so frustrating, too, because they managed to still get rewarded for this behavior in the end by releasing V-Rising - see all those people praising how the combat feels in that game? 

I'll fucking bet. I felt that same way when I first experienced it in Bloodline Champions, and I felt it all over again when I relived it in Battlerite during the early days when it was a glorious rise from the ashes. I'm sure there is more to V-Rising as a game, but without the combat they practically lifted directly from the game they abandoned I promise you it would not have been nearly as successful.

TLDR - I would love to recommend you this game. If it was in the hands of another studio, I probably would be wholeheartedly singing praises for it and would fall over myself in my haste to recommend it to literally anybody who would listen. But unfortunately, the game that I would - to this day! - call the definitive skill based PvP arena experience is in the hands of a company who doesn't care enough to maintain it. So Battlerite died just like Bloodline Champions did before it, and this time Stunlock Studios doesn't have the excuse of a 'restrictive publisher' to hide behind.

We live in a world where not enough people hate Stunlock Studios for what they did. I just hope to do my part in fixing that.

Hey you, person reading this, yeah you.. I believe my Review will be helpful to you, if you care to read.

SEPTEMBER 2026 UPDATE!!

I wrote this review a long, long time ago, but I don't want to change it because I believe everything I wrote back then still applies to the game today! The only update I wanted to make for those of you interested, to my surprise! I came back to the game because I saw that Ranked League resets began happening this year, and WOW the game is POPPING again!

I'll start with the TL:DR Version:

If you think you've ever enjoyed any sort of PvP in an online game before, TRY IT. Simple, as I understand the game is free, it is definitely unlike any other game you've played before (Unless you've played Bloodline Champions in which case it is as good or better and extremely similar), it doesn't take too long to understand the basics, and there is currently a healthy population of players so qeue times are almost always under 1min even 24 hours a day. The absolute worst that can happen is you play the game for a few hours and decide that it's not for you, but even then you won't regret trying it because it was a completely new experience and you will have the knowledge that such a type of game exists in the world, which I promise you is worthy of knowing and feeling if you are into PvP of any sort. 

If I've managed to catch your attention enough to download the game, here are a few very quick tips (under 5min) on how to make your gaming experience better once you are inside:

1. Go to Options > General > Uncheck Camera Lock (You want it off so you can move your mouse/screen more freely)
2. Enable Chat obviously and disable profanity filter.
3. Interrupt on move is a personal preference feature that will vary from player to player so just test it out (Mine is Off)
4. Adjust your HUD Scale to match your Monitor Resolution (I play on a 4K Monitor so I have mine set at highest 2.0)
5. Razer Chroma is really cool Feature in this game if you have any Razer products definitely leave enabled.
6. Go to Options > Controls > You can customize your abilities however you like (Mine are set to Q,E,R,F and Special Abilities are set to my Extra Razer Mouse Buttons)
7. The little Exclamation Mark ! On the bottom of Main Menu will let you collect Chests and such for Free Loot in game. 
8. Once you've picked a Champion you like visit their page under the Collections Tab and configure yourself a customized personal "Loadout" Which is like a "Talent Tree" in other games that will allow you to play your champion your own style.
9. I Highly recommend playing against Bots/AI at first because fighting against other players right off the bat can be rather discouraging, especially when fighting against the Bots in this game can be a surprisingly Fun/Challenging (Against higher difficulty Bots) experience. I have an 80-90% Win-Rate on some Champions in PvP and I still lose to the Hard level bots occassionally. 
10. If you don't already, Use a LAN Cable.. this is not a game you wanna play over WiFi, latency matters.

Now that I've gotten all that out of the way, here is my Actual Review:

I should at first mention a couple of things, such as that I am currently writing this Review during a battle between Twitch/Battlerite for some Twitch Loot Chest issues I have experienced while purchasing Gems for Battlerite and yet my Review will still be overwhelmingly positive despite that fact. This is my very first Review ever written about a video game, at least on Steam, (Hell I don't even like Steam the only reason I use Steam is because of Battlerite), and I have played enough Video Games competitively in my 28 years to probably have written many great reviews and guides or even become a famous streamer by now, but I have not done any of those things because I never felt the need to.. until now, Battlerite is a game that deserves my input to be seen by the public, you!

My opinion is based on my rather thorough experience of online PvP gaming, and my opinion is that Battlerite (+BLC) is the platform for the #1 Best PvP Game ever created. There are no other games exactly like it, although if I had to try my best to explain what it is like; it is like if you were to take the concept of World of Warcraft Arena, use the camera style perspective of Path of Exiles, and the combat system of Smite all mixed into one game.

Essentially the game is just a series of 2v2 / 3v3 Arena Matches that closely resemble the same way World of Warcraft Arena works. However, it does everything right that a game like World of Warcraft does wrong. A few examples would be that there is no such thing as Gear in the game, all Champions are equal and upgradeable/purchased items are Cosmetic Only. The playing field is as balanced as PvP can be, granted some champions will always fare better than others in any type of PvP environment, its the nature of the beast, but I truly believe that no other game can close to achieving the type of balance Battlerite can provide, mainly because it is Balance BASED on Skill. 

The easiest way I think I can explain what I mean is this, Battlerite is one of the only games I have ever played where a Player with High enough Skill can actually 1v3 and come out a Victor. In almost all other games, except for Smite for example (which is why I still hold Smite as a high competitor to Battlerite and bolst their similiarities in combat style), being outnumbered generally means certain death. There's really nothing a player can do 1v3 to come out victorious, but in Battlerite if the person is talented enough at the Champion they are playing (whichever champion that may be) they can actually win a 1v3 or a 1v2 battle and pull off some amazing stunts that are spectacles to watch, I have seen it before in my own eyes, and even occasionally had the pleasure of experiencing it myself. 

A few more examples I would like to share include the fact that every single Round in a Match of Battlerite is extremely intense. (I mean generally speaking if you aren't facing people or bots much much lower skilled than you) When I play Battlerite my heart is racing over 90% of the time, it is all stressful, exhausting, and exhilirating. No other game I've ever played has provided me with such consistent adrenaline as Battlerite PvP. This almost makes playing for long hours difficult because after enough rounds you feel depleted. It makes Winning feel incredibly rewarding, almost unlike any other game, and it makes losing really difficult to bare as well... however, one of the best and most amazing things about Battlerite is the fact that YOU KNOW EXACTLY when you make a mistake that gives you the Loss. It's not like other PvP games where you can blame CC's, or this or that, in Battlerite with the right amount of coordination every single CC can be dodged, parried, reflected, blocked, etc.. and you have to aim every single attack.. so if you mess up and miss an important ability, or if you accidentally waste your parry/reflect at the wrong time YOU WILL get punished for it, but when you ultimately lose the match you will know exactly why you messed up and how you can improve for next time... and over time you learn and get better at it.. its quite a thing I tell you!

In Battlerite there are tons of epic moments, many matches that start off as a 3v3 end up in a 2v2 and then a 1v1 where the last 2 remaining survivors of each team are duking it out trying to bring their team the Win! It's so intense. The craziest is when in the end both players die at the exact same time and you can actually get a DRAW! That's right, if both players die from each-other's final ability because that's how close the match is, it becomes a DRAW and the game goes into overtime and gives you another round to battle it out. I don't know many games that are so fair in PvP as to allow for that to even happen, but when it does (and I've seen it) it's a memorable experience for both teams that they won't soon forget!

Battlerite is an amazing game. Since it's free-to-play I can't NOT recommend it. The most fun elements of a MOBA are neatly packed in a polished, skill-based, well-balanced game with a lot of depth. If you need more convincing than that, I guess I'll do a Pros/Cons list.

[h1] Pros [/h1]

[list]
[*]Fast-paced, reactive and smooth as f**k. Movement is with WASD, which feels so much better than for example LoL's right-click movement. The number of abilites (5 base and 4 "charged") add more depth to the fights than League can accomplish while still keeping the UI much cleaner than something like WoW arena.

[*]Skill-based and very competetive. Every ability is a skillshot. This also rewards dodging skills. You can climb the ladder by simply being good at the game. Not too much emphasis is put on team-mates and after a loss, you usually feel like you could have carried if you had played better.

[*]Amazing balance. All champions are used at the top level, and most are used in tournaments. You can play whoever you want and never feel at a general disadvantage.

[*]Not team comp dependent. Since all team comps are more or less viable (of course, bad and good matchups still exist), you are never forced into playing a role you don't like. You can literally OTP in this game and there will be no one to flame you, and no games lost because of it.

[*]Supports are actually interesting to play and one of the most important archetypes. Say goodbye to LoL's warding, gold-starved CC-bots with questionable contribution and skill ceiling. In Battlerite, supports offer the same healing and crowd control as in other games, but they also dish out a GOOD deal of damage, depending on how you play them. I can assure you, you will have a better experience with supports in this game than in any other.

[*]Good payment model. Champions are earned through playing, or can be bought with real money at a very reasonable price (27.99€ for all current and future champions, or smaller one-time purchases for individual champions). By the time you have truly learnt the champions you own from the start (you get 4 for free, plus a weekly F2P-rotation) you will have earned enough gold to buy, I daresay, almost all others. Even cosmetics can be earned relatively fast through simply playing the game, without paying.

[*]Friendly and outreaching developers who respond to feedback quickly, listen to the community and are open as to what they are currently working on for the game.

[*]The game is growing. F2P was recently released and more and more players are discovering this game.
[/list]

[h1] Cons [/h1]

[list]
[*]Lack of social features. There is no global chat, so your social experience is largely dependent on SoloQ/IRL friends/forums. The devs are however working to improve this as we speak. For me, it is not a big issue, but it might be for some people.

[*]The matchmaking can be a bit off at the VERY top level. Since the playerbase up there is not very big, to avoid long queues, sometimes there can be matches with people of very different skill levels. However, this only really applies to the top 100-300 people in the world, and is not a big problem for the game as a whole, and definately not to beginners. 

[*]The game is very competetive. Yes, I'm putting this as a Con as well because some people might be put off by the amount of concentration it takes to do well. Part of what makes the game so good, the lack of downtime between fights, also means that you will constantly be on your toes. If you're not into competetive PvP this might be something you should know.

[*]After a few hundred hours, you begin to feel the need for more champions. However, the amount of time it takes to master a champion is so large that me, with my 600 hours, only consider myself good with a few of them. What I mean when I say "need more champions" is that matches can sometimes feel very much alike, since there isn't as much champion diversity as in other games. More champions are being released at a decent pace, though.
[/list]

So, do I recommend playing Battlerite?

Hell yes.

Legit one of the best PvP games of all time, at the very least one of the greats in the MOBA space. The playerbase is still OK but sadly the devs have ceased development. One of the biggest what-ifs in gaming for me, they had one of the the most well rounded competitive and balanced PvP games on their hands but ultimately the studio's own questionable decisions as well some things outside of their control ultimately led to them dropping support for the game.

It really is a unique game but if i had to try and explain it then think LoL/Dota/HoTs gameplay with WASD movement instead of mouse and stripped down into pure arena brawling with no creeps, towers and objectives ect. Now having extra depth like that is great and works for those games, but Battlerite was a fresh experience because it was constant fighting. You thought about your team composition against the enemy and strategized the game accordingly, no early game and late game Heroes, just what character you picked and how you play it against what the enemy have and around your teammates picks.

Quick reflexes were rewarded, mastery of Hero was rewarded, game knowledge was rewarded all the things you want in a competitive game, the skill floor wasn't so exponential you couldn't understand the basics of the game as a new player but the skill ceiling was through the roof at the high levels of play.

The game isn't dead but it's hard to commit to a game you know will receive no new content or support, when all is said and done the game is really good, i miss it a lot and wish it took off more. I'm eagerly awaiting something similar to emerge with the same level of polish that Battlerite had, but for now it remains a real gem of a game that never got to truly shine,

[h1]The Lore[/h1]
Just recently the development team [i]Stunlock Studios[/i](SLS) released a [url=https://lore.battlerite.com/]Book of Lore[/url] for the Battlerite universe.
Up until now, it doesn't feature a lot of background information on our dear champions, but I am positive that this will be extended in the future.
However, if you don't want to go looking at slightly external sources, as the book is sadly not accessible from directly in the game, you will have to listen to the voice lines and figure out what little meaning they have.

[h1]The Arenas[/h1]
There are a bunch of arenas featured. Some in day- and night-versions to give off a different vibe.
Still, the more important aspects of them are the tactical possibilities they offer. Some of them have more open space than others and therefore better lines of sight. In the end, it will be up to you to use and abuse the layout to your advantage.
Lastly, there is a feature, that lets you chose up to 5 arenas which you don't want to play in. Yet, it is kind of tricky to find in the current UI - you have to go into a champion selection and use the settings at the top.
I'm giving you this last bit of information because my friends and I had some days where we would play the same arena over and over again, which gets a little stale.

[h1]The UI[/h1]
So, I really have to put this in here...
Because the "new" UI is a real downgrade over the one they had back in Early Access. It has been said so many time by big parts of the community before, but nothing has changed yet.
I think by now most players are used to navigating through endless menus to get to where they want to be. But it's definitely not a great user experience.

[h1]The Champions[/h1]
As this is a "hero-based" game, the champions obviously make up one of the cornerstones of the action.
Nonetheless, there is no need to worry here. Because our cast consists of male, female, young and old and even a few things from farther down the nether realm.
They are grouped into melee, ranged and support. The latter having the ability to actively heal their teammates, while the former may have some kind of self-sustain.
The chances are good that you will find someone fitting for you. But, for a beginner 27 champions, each with 9 abilities is probably a lot to handle. But don't worry. Learning is half the fun.

[h1]The Gameplay[/h1]
Now, at last, we are at the core, the essence, the heart of the sport.
After you’ve chosen your champion, you either queue up for a 3v3 or 2v2 or maybe even a Duel. But let me warn you - the game is balanced around the former. Therefore you may have some problems with the other modes depending on the picks.
Then you enter the arena. There you will be able to select your [i]battle rites[/i] - these enable you to create your own build for your alter ego in the arena. You can either play with the default ones or create up to three custom sets in the lobby.
Lastly, after a sheer endless amount of waiting, you will be able to finally enter the arena and face your foes in a best-of-5 match.
What you will realize though, is that there is more to the field then just you and your foes. In the middle is a circle which fills up and spawns a big orb, with smaller green and orange orbs at the side walls.
Obviously, your main objective is to defeat every enemy player, but for that, it is important to control all the orbs which will offer health (green), energy (orange) or even both (middle orb) for you and your team.
Now I said that there is a resource called energy in the game. Earlier I also mentioned every champion has 9 abilities.

Let me break that down:
[list]
[*][b]LMB:[/b] your basic attack, which can have a [i]charge[/i] empowering the next hit with it - so aim well not to miss it.
[*][b]RMB:[/b] often a low cooldown, signature damage ability or heal for supports - use it often and use it well.
[*][b]E:[/b] hard to generalize but mostly an AoE ability.
[*][b]Space:[/b] this is generally a movement ability, or [i]escape[/i] - so you should use it like this and not waste it to engage with.
[*][b]Q:[b] the counter (with exceptions) and arguably most important move - refrain from hitting them.
[*][b]R:[/b] this skill always uses energy and mostly has some defensive properties to it - use it smartly.
[*][b]F:[/b] your ultimate trademark move. It depletes your whole energy but can be an absolute game changer. Mind, however, that it can be countered like everything else.
[*][b]Shift:[/b] offers you access to your [i]EX-abilities[/i] which are alternate versions of your base abilities with an energy cost to them. Learn to use them just like all the others.
[/list]

Oh and also: if you go into the game coming from my review - don't ask "who do we focus?". In this game you focus whoever is vulnerable, which means no escape, no counter and maybe out of position.

[h1]The Visuals[/h1]
With these stylised games, it's always a matter of taste but I really enjoy the look of the game.
Animations are a) great looking and b) precise, which adds to the general excellent feel of being in control.
Another point I particularly like are the skins. Firstly, they can be obtained through gameplay with relative ease and secondly, there are some real stunners to be had.

[h1]The Sound[/h1]
Audio cues are a really important gameplay aspect. They can tell you where some invisible characters are hiding or which attack is coming your way. The most important warning being the ultimate voice lines, where everyone has a specific thing to say.
Adding to that are the [i]flavor[/i] lines, that every voice actor perfectly performed. As mentioned before they might open up a little bit of insight on your hero.

[h1]The Verdict[/h1]
In the end, I want to address the price of the game, as it is f2p you will have a lot of grinding to do, to unlock every champion.
That's why I recommend you try it out for free and if you like it get the All Champions Pack, preferably on a sale. That way you have your coins to buy chests to unlock skins, since buying these for gems aka real money currency is overpriced as fuck.
Nevertheless you truly [i]should[/i] give this game a try, because it is great fun with a lot of stuff to learn and master and a blood-pumping intensity that might leave you exhausted.

I hope this review helped you in deciding to give this game a try and if you liked my review, I would be grateful for a 'thumbs up', if you didn't like it, you can give me a 'thumbs down' but I would be glad to hear your opinion on what you didn't like.

I cannot recommend this game enough. 
Battlerite is a MOBA in it's purest form, with no towers, creeps, last hits, gold, items, leveling, snowballing, 40 minute matches or any of the other unnessecary parts of popular MOBAs like DotA, LoL, or Smite.
Battlerite takes the fun part of the game, the fights, and creates a game solely based around that and that alone. 
2 minute rounds, with a first to 3 match system. Available in 2v2 or 3v3 formats. It's quick and easy, and you don't have to set aside time to commit just to playing it. 

Let's go over what makes this game so great:
Short matches. In just 40 hours I have almost almost 200 matches played. With 40 hours in regular MOBAs you would probably have less than 100 with that time.

Pure skill based combat. In this game, there's almost always room to improve. In almost every situation it's a case of "I could have done better there" rather than "This champion is OP" or "He's too fed FF @ 20." With enough practice, you can climb by yourself just by carrying with skill.

Every champion is viable. This sounds completely untrue, but believe me, you can one trick pony in this game and do well. Every champion will do well if you can do well as that champion.

A focus on individual skill. Instead of relying on four other teammates, you only need to rely on one, and at most, two. Even then you don't have to rely on them. As stated previously, if you're good enough, you can 1v2 on your own.

No specific roles. For example: 
Melee does not mean "Tank"
Ranged does not mean "DPS" 
Support does not mean "Healer"
Each role is just a vague description. Support can still do damage, and tanks don't exist. No one is meant to take damage here.

9 different skills and they're all skillshots. This is where a lot of the depth of the game comes in. Nothing is just a point and click stun, or an unavoidable one shot. Everything must be aimed, and everything can be dodged.


Of course, nothing is perfect. There are some cons I find to this game as well.
Steep learning curve. The first few matches a new player has will be tough, you'll barely understand your character, and have no idea how to play against the others. This makes matches incredibly tough. If you're new to the game and are reading this, visit https://www.battlecrank.com/start/ to get some helpful information.

The game is actually $30. Of course, no one is saying you HAVE to buy the Champions pack, but you really should. There's no disadvantage for not owning it, but it's a nice thing to have. If you enjoy the game it should definitely be your next purchase.

Lack of global chat. Such a minor inconvience, but it's understandable, right?


TL;DR play the game. It's fair, fun, and a great experience.

I have spent nearly 500 hours in this title, I started playing back when it was in beta. The game started out great, needed some work of course, but stunlock made the right choices and their game turned out very unique and HIGHLY skill based. I'm making this in comparison to other moba genres like dota and league of legends*. I'm going to talk about why i think battlerite died and what i think they could have done better in order to keep this amazing style alive.

I noticed that the game's player base was significantly low and i dont blame SLS (stunlock studios) for trying to bump up their player base by making updates. however, these updates they were adding , werent healthy for the game's future.
I'v noticed a trend over the past 6 or so years , that whenever a game that has unique qualities and some great fundamental mechanics but includes different "classes" "characters" or "champions", the developers strive to keep adding more and more characters to their roster similar to League of legends, overwatch, dota, paladins, etc.

 but have you noticed that some games havent died out? take a look at team fortress two. This beauty of a game hasn't received many updates, but because they haven't ADDED more characters and complicated mechanics that could potentially be too hard to balance, they have a balanced game that is very consistent and is loved by many to this day.

The reason i think the player base of battlerite died was because they:
1) pumped out character after character without thinking about fine tuning balance before hand.
2)catered to the paying player with more cosmetics, frequent events and a battlepass. 
3) most importantly, they didnt stay consistent with their base game's mechanics and style.

Let's talk about the first reason. 
A lot of other reviews said similar things, but the first thing people jump to is always about "greedy" developers and a big money sink. But you have to realise that SLS still created this game and had a dream from the beginning, they had this idea for battlerite and they gave it life so we can't deny the fact that they still created a wonderful game. 

Things started to go downhill when the player base was fluctuating from other game's popularity or from new games being released. SLS panicked, and thought their game was going to die out so they added even more champions but without thinking about their RETURNING players. this turned into some heavy meta's and a  constantly shifting one because stuff was not getting balanced in the way it should have, before adding more mechanics and more characters. 

So the returning players such as myself , came back to a completely different game that had felt completely different from when i started, forcing me to drop certain characters because they are countered to hard by other picks or just not up to snuff compared to some other counterparts. f/e destiny on release, she had broken hit boxes and had some over tuned damage on her rmb, so SLS said "oh this is way too strong" instead of minorly adjusting things, she ended up being god awful compared to other common picks like jumong because she got nerfed so hard - the meta shifted, then another character got released and destiny's play rate went way down. 

TLDR the more characters you add, the harder it is to stay consistent in balancing your  roster. - creating metas-

Secondly im going to talk about the main issue that a lot of players had. SLS created a game and of course wanted to earn some money for it, hence their lootbox systems creation and it actually being great. the event's were really fun and unique and people are willing to pay for their skins. 

Things went wrong the moment battlerite turned into a F2P game. Battlerite royale came out and most players moved over to it and/or tried it out. It was fun and accepted in the community because it was THE first moba battleroyale. but the issue is, the arena community died... the people that still wanted to go back and play arena were met with ONLY the players that grinded the game and were really high level and were good. so new players got smashed going into matchmaking because the player base basically shifted to BRR. so: 
1) Battlerite made free to play
2) BRR released and cost money.
3)Battlerite players moved over.
4) lost interest due to other games taking popularity .
5) the BRR players didnt come back, it isnt the same as Battlerite by any means. different items, different team play, different mechanics.
6) new players of Battlerite were met with a tough matchmaking system because the player base was so low.
7) the players that lost interest try and come back to Battlerite and were met with a low player base, struggling to find a balanced game. so they left.
8) Battlerite died. along with it's pro league.

The third and final reason why i think battlerite died, was because of the inconsistency. The game was meant to be the next generation of Bloodline Champions players. but what we ended up with was a bunch of moba Battleroyale players that threw in a plethora of gimmick items and strange mechanics that could throw RNG into the mix.

Arena had it right. It was fast, skill based, and a unique genre. All it needed to do was to gain loyalty from players that loved that style of game and it definitely could have grown. But as mentioned before, the player base naturally fluctuates based on other games popularity. but instead of catering to the loyal players who love the game for what it is, they  didnt stay consistent and ended up with a game that didnt feel as true to the original intention of its origin.

I will not recommend this game to players looking for a "new style" of moba. they will be met with a brutal matchmaking system due to the low player base and too many champions to get a grasp of and learn how to play as/against as its extremely skill based.

However, If one day a new developer or even Stunlock themselves, decide to revamp this game and make it great again and revive this style/genre i highly recommend players to try it out, and to come back and play.

Much love for this game, and I hope one day to play it again like i used to.

After 250 hours of playing Battlerite, I've decided that it is finally time to write a review for this epic fighting masterpiece. While it has its pros and cons, Battlerite overall is a great game that is well on the way towards its ideal "perfect" state for its Free-To-Play launch. Please keep in mind that this review is based off of my opinions, and my views on the state of the game as a high diamond player.

Pros:

-Amazing gameplay
-Intuitive mechanics
-High skill cap
-Effective counterplay for most scenarios
-Polished game, no-low FPS lag
-Clean and easy to distinguish what is happening
-Large and continuously expanding character roster
-Few cheaters/hackers
-Cool cosmetics
-Decently frequent updates
-Extremely absorbing and addicting
-Easy-to-enter tournaments
-No snowballing (Always room for comeback)
-100% skill and strategy, if you lose, you got outplayed. Maybe a matchup was unfavorable, but you personally could have played better.
-Huge update coming soon (new gamemodes woot)
-Odeum (playback games and post big plays, like an in-game instagram for sick outplays)
-Very few bugs/glitches

Cons:

-Some characters are sometimes a bit too strong/meta
-Small player base (Perhaps the biggest con, while the playerbase is good, matchmaking can sometimes feel way too long for a short 2v2 brawl.)
-Ranking system (Recently got a change, and is a bit better, but still has tons of room for improvement)
-Dev focus (Sometimes, it seems that the Devs are more excited to push out new cosmetics than improve balance or matchmaking)
-Matchmaking (I still dont understand why I play with a bronzie against 2 Champions every now and then)

These are most of the pros/cons I can think of off the top of my head, but overall this game is very fun and well made. Do keep in mind that Battlerite is still in early access, meaning not everything is perfect yet, but hopefully will be by the time of its full release. For $20, you get to play this awesome game many months earlier than the people waiting for F2P, as well as unlocking the full character cast (which means you dont have to grind up to buy characters). I highly reccomend this game to anyone who is at least a bit interested in it/anyone who enjoys MOBAs (Ex: LOL, Dota 2, HOTS, Smite), and give it my rating of 9/10. The Devs have room for improvement, but have already succeeded in making a kickass game for us to enjoy.

When I saw they were releasing a BLC clone, I was skeptical at first.  I already had to watch one of my favorite games die once, and I really didn't want to watch it happen again.

After playing a slew of matches today, I'm incredibly impressed with how they improved (in my opinion) on the formula.

* All champions unlocked.  I feel like this is crucial for new MOBAs these days, and I feel like going with a Hearthstone-esque implementation of reward is really going to help.  It sucks being limited to 4 of 16 champions and feeling gated behind a paywall.  Now you have everything available, and you can dump money into chests for cosmetics if you want.  Now cosmetics are random, but I feel like that's OK.

EDIT - I'm not 100% sure this is how the game will be when it's F2P, and if it is, I hope they have a paid package that is just the same roughly $20 for all champions unlocked forever.  I really don't like champion gating, though I also come from DOTA, so it's a foreign and unwanted concept.

* Daily quests for chests.  I don't know, maybe it's just me, but I love this sort of thing on queued games.  It gives you a reason to experiment with other champions, giving you something to work toward and play the game without fussing over only rating, or some stat-based progression.

* The Battlerites.  Even though I seem to always choose the same ones, that's probably just because I have a specific playstyle.  I love the little flavor these add to the game.

* Simplified Roles:  Support, Melee, Ranged.  No more tank, no more healer.  Support has a heal, but it's on a cooldown instead of being spammable.  In my opinion, this means they have to be more clutch, less spam.

* You face where your mouse points, not where you are WASDing.  I don't know if there's back attack modifiers in this game, but this just feels a lot cleaner.  Maybe it made the game more professional before, but I like this change.

* Arena design.  Maybe I'm forgetting, but I feel like old BLC arenas were mostly open area, with maybe a couple LoS opportunities in one or two of them on the sides.  Battlerite feels, by and large, like a smaller central area with more juking potential, which is good because you often want to be interacting with that environment.  Which brings me to

* Environment interaction.  Receiving additional benefits when capitalizing on positioning feels really good, and I think adds to the flow of the game.

* Cracking the energy ball to receive the boost.  I like the strategy this adds to a fight, since you don't just run in and get free energy.  You can make big plays off of a team you know is going to huddle as soon as it pops (which might not be the best players on the team, but you won't always be in top tier gaming).

* Health/energy pickups around the arena.  I haven't programmed myself to look for these yet, but with the reduced amount of spammed healing available, these really help you sustain if you pay attention.  Gives it a bit more of an FPS arena feel, and I really like that.

* Performance.  This game runs smoothly (on low, mind you) on my 4 year old gaming laptop.  It can't run most games these days, but it can run Battlerite, and that makes me incredibly happy.

Cons?  I hate only showering a game with praise, but I haven't seen any balance issues of yet.  Part of that is because I don't fully know all of the new nuances of each champion, and I'm not going to jump to conclusions.  Everything has felt manageable so far as long as I don't waste my toolset.  If I die, I often did something dumb.  If I'm out of position, again, I misplayed.

It's almost exactly what I wanted out of a BLC reboot.  Plays incredibly smoothly, feels great, insanely fun.  And *somehow*, I have yet to run into a poor attitude. Everyone has been nice so far.  Maybe it's the thrill of having this sort of game back in the mix, but I've made some doozie mistakes, and still when I'm like "Sorry about that", it's "np".  And if you don't want to hear a tirade, you can completely disable chat.

I thought of a con:

* No scenarios.  I lived for BLC scenarios back when people queued for them.  The additional objectives made it feel more engaging for me than just an arena brawler, but I understand that they are refining their focus this time around.  If Scenarios are released in the future, I'm going to scream like a school girl at a One Direction concert.  If not, this game is still incredible.

If you loved BLC, pick up this game right now.

If you stopped playing BLC because of the progression garbage added to the game and the money grab that is champion pool availability lottery, pick up this game because there is none of that (and I hope that stays, even for newly released champions).

If you have no idea what BLC is but you are hesitant because of DOTA and LoL, keep an eye on this game.  Watch some videos, read more reviews, and understand that it is not those games.  No 60 minutes slow downhill farming loss.  No intense vitriol for minutes on end because everyone is stuck in a losing scenario and can't get out. [h1]What is Battlerite?[/h1]

Battlerite is a hybrid somewhere between Dota 2 and World of Warcraft style Battlegrounds - you take on opponents in 2v2 and 3v3 arena-style skirmishes and try to be the last team standing (after a best of 5 match).  From Dota 2 it borrows maticulous hero balance, movement/camera mechanics, and a handful of thought-out abilities for each playable character.  From WoW Battlegrounds it borrows a focus on pure PvP; there are no objectives here other than defeat your opponent.  What is unique to Battlerite is the major importance of movement; I've found quick reaction time and mobility to be one of the most necessary skills to succeed here in order to dodge enemy attacks, zone enemy teams/players, and land powerful abilities. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Gameplay is fast, fluid, and has an incredibly high skill ceiling that rewards practice, hero/ability knowledge, and mechanical ability.  The devs are constantly tweaking, balancing, and updating this game which has consistently received excellent support. 

[h1]Dev Support / Early Access[/h1]

Battlerite is currently (as of June 27, 2017) an Early Access title, but don't let that deter you. Battlerite is one of the most well-developed and supported games I've ever played in early access and I'm often highly critical of the early access model.  Note that, while the game is available for purchase during early access, it will be free when it hits release.  You hear "free-to-play" and immediately have fears of "pay-to-win"? You (probably) don't. While the exact model of the F2P release are somewhat unclear, at worst, it will function like League of Legends; starting with a limited pool of champions requiring you to either play (or pay) to unlock more, and any other purchases being cosmetics. Note that any Early Access purchasers will have all current and future champions unlocked.

[h1]Verdict:[/h1] 

I [b]definitely recommend, 7.5/10[/b] anyone with interest in this game (or players of Dota 2 or WoW Battlegrounds) to pick it up when it goes free upon release.  If the game seems like something you're particularly interested in, it's worth the $20 non-sale price; but on sale (or when free to play) its an even better buy.  My only major concern with the title, in addition to some questions about the F2P model, is the small player-base. While you won't have trouble finding games quickly you'll an average 3,000 players online at a time and see repeat players often.  Hopefully more will be playing when it goes free!
